Cut a new release for xspct_scan and push it to both remotes.

## Steps (run in order — stop and report on failure)

### 1. Determine the new version

Read the current version from `pyproject.toml` (`[project].version`). Look at
`docs/changelog.md`'s `## Unreleased` section and `git log --oneline <last-tag>..HEAD`
to see what changed, then propose a new version following semver (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`):

- `MAJOR` — breaking changes (commits with `!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer)
- `MINOR` — new `feat` commits, no breaking changes
- `PATCH` — only `fix`/`docs`/`refactor`/`test`/`perf`/`build`/`ci`/`chore`

Ask the user to confirm the proposed version (or supply their own) before proceeding.

### 2. Update the changelog

`CHANGELOG.md` is a symlink to `docs/changelog.md` — edit `docs/changelog.md` only.

- Rename the `## Unreleased` heading to `## X.Y.Z — YYYY-MM-DD` (today's date).
- Add a fresh empty `## Unreleased` heading above it, so future work has
  somewhere to land.
- Keep the existing `### Added` / `### Fixed` / etc. subsections and bullets
  as-is — do not rewrite prior entries.
- If the `## Unreleased` section is empty, stop and ask the user what should
  go in the release notes before continuing.

### 3. Bump the version

Update `version = "..."` in `pyproject.toml` to `X.Y.Z`. This is the single
source of truth — `__version__` in `src/xspct_scan/__init__.py` derives it via
`importlib.metadata` at runtime, nothing else needs editing.

### 4. Regenerate the SBOM

The version bump changes `bom.json`'s own component entry, so it must be
regenerated every release:

```bash
.venv/bin/cyclonedx-py environment --of JSON -o bom.json
```
Report the number of components listed and confirm `bom.json` now reflects
version `X.Y.Z`.

### 5. Run the pre-flight checks

```bash
.venv/bin/ruff check src/ tests/
.venv/bin/reuse lint
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --tb=short
```
Stop and report if any of these fail. Do not proceed to committing on failure.

### 6. Stage and commit

```bash
git add pyproject.toml docs/changelog.md bom.json
git commit -S -m "chore(release): X.Y.Z"
```
Use the confirmed version number in place of `X.Y.Z`. Remind the user to
verify their GPG key is available (`gpg --list-secret-keys`) if signing fails.

### 7. Tag

```bash
git tag -s X.Y.Z -m "X.Y.Z"
```

### 8. Push to both remotes

This repo has two remotes — `origin` (GitLab) and `github` (GitHub). Push the
branch and the tag to both:

```bash
git push origin HEAD
git push origin X.Y.Z
git push github HEAD
git push github X.Y.Z
```

Report the result of each push. If one remote rejects the push (e.g. branch
protection, diverged history), **stop** and surface the error instead of
retrying with `--force`.

## Hard rules

- **Never** invent changelog entries — only reorganize/date what's already
  under `## Unreleased`.
- **Never** include "generated by", "co-authored by", or any AI attribution
  in the commit or tag message.
- Commit and tag **must** be GPG-signed (`-S` / `-s`).
- Do not use `--force` on any push in this workflow.
- Confirm the version number with the user before committing/tagging — it
  cannot be easily changed once pushed.
